source_refs.note: Exercise 12.1, Question 4 (book page 230): twelve limits, parts (i)-(xii), mostly sin(theta)/theta. Key PDF 310 skips (viii) (correct p^2/q^2); all other key answers agree. Solution book PDF 1067-1079.

blocks.explanation:
\(x = 0\) rakhne par \(\sin 0/0 = 0/0\) aata hai, undecided.
Sine ke andar angle \(5x\) hai lekin neeche sirf \(x\). Standard limit tab lagta hai jab dono ek jaise hon.
Plan: upar neeche \(5\) se multiply kar ke neeche bhi \(5x\) banayenge, phir \(\lim \frac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\) lagayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{\sin 5x}{x}\), \(x \to 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

Neeche ko angle ke barabar banayein
\[\frac{\sin 5x}{x} = 5 \cdot \frac{\sin 5x}{5x}\]
Kyun: Upar aur neeche dono ko \(5\) se multiply kiya, is liye value wohi hai. Ab neeche bhi \(5x\) hai, bilkul sine ke andar jaisa. Extra \(5\) bahar aa gaya.

Standard limit lagayein
\[\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin 5x}{x} = 5 \lim_{5x \to 0} \frac{\sin 5x}{5x}\]
\[= 5(1) = 5\]
Kyun: \(\theta = 5x\) maan lein. Jab \(x \to 0\) to \(\theta = 5x \to 0\) bhi. Is liye \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta} \to 1\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{\sin 5x}{x}\) mein \(x\) "kaat" kar \(\sin 5\) likhna bilkul ghalat hai; \(\sin\) ke andar wala \(x\) bahar ke \(x\) se kat nahi sakta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 0.01:\ \frac{\sin 0.05}{0.01} \approx 4.998\]
Kyun: Calculator radian mode mein rakh kar check kiya; jawab \(5\) ke qareeb hai.

blocks.explanation:
Is sawal ki khaas baat: angle \(x\) degree mein hai, jabke standard limit sirf radians mein sahi hai.
Plan: \(x^{\circ}\) ko radians mein badlenge (\(x^{\circ} = \frac{\pi x}{180}\) rad), neeche ko us angle ke barabar banayenge, phir \(\lim \frac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{\sin x^{\circ}}{x}\), \(x \to 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

Degree ko radian mein badlein
\[x^{\circ} = \frac{\pi x}{180} \text{ rad}\]
\[\frac{\sin x^{\circ}}{x} = \frac{\sin \dfrac{\pi x}{180}}{x}\]
Kyun: \(180^{\circ} = \pi\) radian, is liye \(1^{\circ} = \frac{\pi}{180}\) radian, aur \(x^{\circ} = \frac{\pi x}{180}\) radian. Standard limit ka saboot (12.2.9) sector ke area se tha jo radian mein hi hota hai; is liye degree mein woh \(1\) nahi deta.

Neeche ko angle ke barabar banayein
\[= \frac{\pi}{180} \cdot \frac{\sin \dfrac{\pi x}{180}}{\dfrac{\pi x}{180}}\]
Kyun: Upar aur neeche ko \(\frac{\pi}{180}\) se multiply kiya; value wohi rahi, aur ab neeche bhi wohi angle hai jo sine ke andar.

Standard limit lagayein
\[\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin x^{\circ}}{x} = \frac{\pi}{180}(1)\]
\[= \frac{\pi}{180}\]
Kyun: \(x \to 0\) ho to \(\theta = \frac{\pi x}{180} \to 0\), is liye \(\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta} \to 1\).
Dhyan dein: Jawab \(1\) likhna aam ghalti hai. Degree wale angle mein hamesha \(\frac{\pi}{180}\) ka factor aata hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 0.01:\ \frac{\sin (0.01^{\circ})}{0.01} \approx 0.0174533\]
\[\frac{\pi}{180} \approx 0.0174533\]
Kyun: Calculator degree mode mein \(\sin(0.01^{\circ})\) nikal kar dekha; dono values mil gayin.

blocks.explanation:
\(\theta = 0\) par upar \(1 - 1 = 0\) aur neeche \(\sin 0 = 0\): \(0/0\).
Book ki Example 9 jaisa tareeqa: \(1 - \cos \theta\) ko \(1 + \cos \theta\) se multiply karo to \(\sin^2 \theta\) ban jata hai.
Plan: multiply, identity lagana, \(\sin \theta\) kaatna, phir value rakhna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{1 - \cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\), \(\theta \to 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: \(\dfrac{1 + \cos \theta}{1 + \cos \theta}\) se multiply kar ke \(\sin^2 \theta\) banana, phir kaatna.

Upar aur neeche ko \(1 + \cos \theta\) se multiply karein
\[\frac{1 - \cos \theta}{\sin \theta} \cdot \frac{1 + \cos \theta}{1 + \cos \theta} = \frac{1 - \cos^2 \theta}{\sin \theta (1 + \cos \theta)}\]
Kyun: \((1 - \cos \theta)(1 + \cos \theta) = 1 - \cos^2 \theta\), difference of squares. Yeh bilkul rationalise karne jaisa hai jo humne roots ke saath kiya tha.

\(1 - \cos^2 \theta = \sin^2 \theta\) likh kar kaatein
\[= \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\sin \theta (1 + \cos \theta)}\]
\[= \frac{\sin \theta}{1 + \cos \theta}\]
Kyun: \(\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = 1\) wali identity. Phir upar ke \(\sin^2 \theta\) mein se ek \(\sin \theta\) neeche wale ke saath kat gaya; \(\theta \to 0\) mein \(\theta \ne 0\), is liye \(\sin \theta \ne 0\).

\(\theta = 0\) rakhein
\[\lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{\sin \theta}{1 + \cos \theta} = \frac{0}{1 + 1}\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: Ab neeche \(2\) hai, zero nahi; is liye seedha value rakh sakte hain. Upar \(0\), neeche \(2\): jawab \(0\).
Dhyan dein: \(0/2 = 0\) mukammal jawab hai; is ko undecided na samjhein.

Tasdeeq
\[\theta = 0.01:\ \frac{1 - \cos 0.01}{\sin 0.01} \approx 0.005\]
Kyun: Zero ke qareeb hai; jaise jaise \(\theta\) chhota hoga yeh aur chhota hota jayega.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iv) Evaluate the following limits: \(\lim\limits_{x \to \pi} \frac{\sin x}{\pi - x}\).
blocks.explanation:
\(x = \pi\) par \(\sin \pi = 0\) aur \(\pi - \pi = 0\): \(0/0\).
Lekin yahan \(x\) zero ki taraf nahi, \(\pi\) ki taraf ja raha hai; standard limit seedha nahi lagta.
Plan: naya variable \(t = \pi - x\) lenge (jo zero ki taraf jayega), \(\sin(\pi - t) = \sin t\) lagayenge, phir standard limit.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{\sin x}{\pi - x}\), \(x \to \pi\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

Variable badlein
\[t = \pi - x \Rightarrow x = \pi - t\]
\[x \to \pi \Rightarrow t \to 0\]
Kyun: Standard limit ko aisa angle chahiye jo zero ki taraf jaye. Neeche \(\pi - x\) pehle se maujood hai aur woh zero ki taraf hi ja raha hai, is liye usi ko \(t\) bana diya.

Sine ko naye variable mein likhein
\[\sin x = \sin(\pi - t) = \sin t\]
Kyun: \(\pi - t\) (yani \(180^{\circ} - t\)) second quadrant mein hai jahan sine positive hai, aur allied angle ke qanoon se \(\sin(\pi - t) = \sin t\).

Standard limit lagayein
\[\lim_{x \to \pi} \frac{\sin x}{\pi - x} = \lim_{t \to 0} \frac{\sin t}{t}\]
\[= 1\]
Kyun: Ab sine ke andar bhi \(t\) aur neeche bhi \(t\), aur \(t \to 0\). Dono shartein poori.
Dhyan dein: \(x \to \pi\) wale sawal mein \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\) jaisa sochna ghalat hai; pehle variable shift karna zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \pi - 0.01:\ \frac{\sin(\pi - 0.01)}{0.01} \approx 0.99998\]
Kyun: \(1\) ke bilkul qareeb.

blocks.prompt: 4 (v) Evaluate the following limits: \(\lim\limits_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin ax}{\sin bx}\).
blocks.explanation:
\(x = 0\) par upar \(\sin 0 = 0\) aur neeche bhi \(0\): \(0/0\). Yahan \(a\) aur \(b\) non-zero constants hain.
Plan: upar aur neeche ko \(x\) se divide karenge, har sine ke neeche us ka apna angle banayenge, phir standard limit do dafa lagayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{\sin ax}{\sin bx}\), \(x \to 0\), \(a, b \ne 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

Har sine ko us ke angle ke saath jorein
\[\frac{\sin ax}{\sin bx} = \frac{a \cdot \dfrac{\sin ax}{ax}}{b \cdot \dfrac{\sin bx}{bx}}\]
Kyun: Pehle upar aur neeche ko \(x\) se divide kiya (value nahi badli). Phir \(\frac{\sin ax}{x}\) ko \(a\) se multiply aur divide kar ke \(a \cdot \frac{\sin ax}{ax}\) banaya; neeche bhi isi tarah \(b \cdot \frac{\sin bx}{bx}\).

Standard limit do dafa lagayein
\[\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin ax}{\sin bx} = \frac{a(1)}{b(1)}\]
\[= \frac{a}{b}\]
Kyun: \(ax \to 0\) aur \(bx \to 0\), is liye dono fractions \(1\) ki taraf jate hain. Neeche \(b \ne 0\), is liye quotient theorem jaiz hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\sin ax / \sin bx\) ko \(\sin(a/b)\) ya \(ax/bx\) "kaat" kar likhna ghalat hai; jawab \(a/b\) standard limit ki wajah se aata hai, kaatne ki wajah se nahi.

Tasdeeq: \(a = 2\), \(b = 1\), \(x = 0.01\)
\[\frac{\sin 0.02}{\sin 0.01} \approx 1.9999\]
Kyun: \(a/b = 2\) ke qareeb. Yeh part (i) se bhi milta hai: \(b = 1\) ho to \(\sin bx \approx x\).

blocks.explanation:
\(x = 0\) par \(0/\tan 0 = 0/0\).
\(\tan\) ka koi alag standard limit humare paas nahi; is liye isay \(\sin\) aur \(\cos\) mein todenge.
Plan: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) likh kar \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\) banayenge, phir standard limit.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{x}{\tan x}\), \(x \to 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

\(\tan\) ko \(\sin\) aur \(\cos\) mein likhein
\[\frac{x}{\tan x} = \frac{x \cos x}{\sin x}\]
\[= \frac{\cos x}{\dfrac{\sin x}{x}}\]
Kyun: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\). Kisi fraction se divide karna us ke ulte (reciprocal) se multiply karna hai, is liye \(\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) se multiply hua. Phir upar aur neeche ko \(x\) se divide kiya taake neeche standard shakal \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\) ban jaye.

Limit lein
\[\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{x}{\tan x} = \frac{\cos 0}{1}\]
\[= 1\]
Kyun: \(\cos x\) har jagah continuous hai, is liye \(\cos x \to \cos 0 = 1\). Neeche \(\frac{\sin x}{x} \to 1\), jo zero nahi.
Dhyan dein: \(\cos 0 = 1\) hai, \(0\) nahi; yeh ghalti aksar jaldi mein hoti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 0.01:\ \frac{0.01}{\tan 0.01} \approx 0.99997\]
Kyun: \(1\) ke bilkul qareeb. Saath hi yaad rakhein: \(\lim \frac{\tan x}{x} = 1\) bhi isi tarah nikalta hai.

blocks.explanation:
\(x = 0\) par upar \(1 - \cos 0 = 1 - 1 = 0\) aur neeche \(0\): \(0/0\).
Upar \(1 - \cos 2x\) ko identity se \(2\sin^2 x\) mein badla ja sakta hai, aur neeche \(x^2\) hai: dono mil kar \(\left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^2\) bana dete hain.
Plan: identity, phir standard limit ka square.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{x^2}\), \(x \to 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

Identity lagayein
\[1 - \cos 2x = 2\sin^2 x\]
\[\frac{1 - \cos 2x}{x^2} = \frac{2\sin^2 x}{x^2}\]
\[= 2\left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^2\]
Kyun: Double angle formula \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\) se \(1 - \cos 2x = 2\sin^2 x\). Phir \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{x^2} = \left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^2\), kyunke \(\frac{a^2}{b^2} = \left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^2\).
Dhyan dein: \(1 - \cos 2x\) ko \(2\sin x\) ya \(\sin^2 2x\) likhna aam ghalti hai; sahi \(2\sin^2 x\) hai.

Limit lein
\[\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos 2x}{x^2} = 2(1)^2\]
\[= 2\]
Kyun: Power theorem: square ka limit = limit ka square. \(\frac{\sin x}{x} \to 1\), is liye \(\left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^2 \to 1\), aur \(2 \times 1 = 2\).

Tasdeeq
\[x = 0.01:\ \frac{1 - \cos 0.02}{0.0001} \approx 1.99993\]
Kyun: \(2\) ke bohat qareeb.

blocks.prompt: 4 (viii) Evaluate the following limits: \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos p\theta}{1 - \cos q\theta}\).
blocks.explanation:
\(\theta = 0\) par upar aur neeche dono \(1 - 1 = 0\): \(0/0\). Yahan \(p\) aur \(q\) non-zero constants hain.
Plan: upar aur neeche dono par \(1 - \cos A = 2\sin^2 \frac{A}{2}\) lagayenge, har sine ke neeche us ka angle banayenge, phir standard limit.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{1 - \cos p\theta}{1 - \cos q\theta}\), \(\theta \to 0\), \(p, q \ne 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

\(1 - \cos A = 2\sin^2 \dfrac{A}{2}\) lagayein
\[\frac{1 - \cos p\theta}{1 - \cos q\theta} = \frac{2\sin^2 \dfrac{p\theta}{2}}{2\sin^2 \dfrac{q\theta}{2}}\]
Kyun: Half angle wali identity \(\cos A = 1 - 2\sin^2 \frac{A}{2}\) se. Upar \(A = p\theta\) aur neeche \(A = q\theta\). Yeh part (vii) wali hi identity hai, bas angle aadha kar ke likhi gayi.

Har sine ko us ke angle ke saath jorein
\[= \frac{\left(\dfrac{\sin (p\theta/2)}{p\theta/2}\right)^2 \dfrac{p^2\theta^2}{4}}{\left(\dfrac{\sin (q\theta/2)}{q\theta/2}\right)^2 \dfrac{q^2\theta^2}{4}}\]
Kyun: Pehle \(2\) aur \(2\) kat gaye. Phir \(\sin^2 \frac{p\theta}{2}\) ko \(\left(\frac{p\theta}{2}\right)^2\) se divide aur multiply kiya, taake standard shakal \(\left(\frac{\sin u}{u}\right)^2\) ban jaye; neeche \(q\) ke saath bhi yahi.

\(\dfrac{\theta^2}{4}\) kaat kar limit lein
\[\lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos p\theta}{1 - \cos q\theta} = \frac{(1)^2 p^2}{(1)^2 q^2}\]
\[= \frac{p^2}{q^2}\]
Kyun: \(\theta \ne 0\), is liye \(\frac{\theta^2}{4}\) upar neeche se kat gaya. \(\frac{p\theta}{2} \to 0\) aur \(\frac{q\theta}{2} \to 0\), is liye dono brackets \(1\) ki taraf jate hain.
Dhyan dein: Jawab \(p/q\) nahi, \(p^2/q^2\) hai; square sine ke square se aata hai.

Tasdeeq: \(p = 2\), \(q = 1\), \(\theta = 0.01\)
\[\frac{1 - \cos 0.02}{1 - \cos 0.01} \approx 3.9999\]
Kyun: \(p^2/q^2 = 4\) ke qareeb. Answer key mein yeh part chhapa hi nahi, is liye yeh tasdeeq aur bhi zaroori hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Answer key part (viii) ko chhod deti hai: (vii) \(2\) ke baad seedha (ix) \(0\) likha hai. Part (viii) ka jawab \(\frac{p^2}{q^2}\) hai.

blocks.explanation:
\(\theta = 0\) par \(0/0\).
Upar do sine hain (\(\sin^2 \theta\)) aur neeche sirf ek \(\theta\). Ek sine ko \(\theta\) ke saath jor denge, doosra akela rahega.
Plan: \(\sin^2 \theta\) ko do hisson mein todna, phir product theorem.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{\sin^2 \theta}{\theta}\), \(\theta \to 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Standard limit (12.2.9) \(\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\), jahan \(\theta\) radians mein ho. Shart yeh hai ke sine ke andar wala angle aur neeche wala hissa bilkul ek jaise hon, aur woh zero ki taraf ja raha ho. Yaad rakhne ka jumla: 'sine ke andar jo, neeche bhi wohi'.

Upar ko do hisson mein torein
\[\frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\theta} = \frac{\sin \theta}{\theta} \cdot \sin \theta\]
Kyun: \(\sin^2 \theta = \sin \theta \times \sin \theta\). Ek \(\sin \theta\) ko \(\theta\) ke upar rakh kar standard shakal bana di, doosra bahar rakh diya.

Product theorem lagayein
\[\lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\theta} = \lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{\sin \theta}{\theta} \cdot \lim_{\theta \to 0} \sin \theta\]
\[= (1)(0) = 0\]
Kyun: Product ka limit = limits ka product. Pehla hissa \(1\) ki taraf, doosra \(\sin 0 = 0\) ki taraf. \(1 \times 0 = 0\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{\sin^2 \theta}{\theta}\) ko \(\left(\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}\right)^2\) samajh kar \(1\) likhna ghalat hai; neeche \(\theta^2\) nahi, sirf \(\theta\) hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\theta = 0.01:\ \frac{\sin^2 0.01}{0.01} \approx 0.01\]
Kyun: Zero ke qareeb, aur \(\theta\) jitna chhota karein yeh utna hi chhota hota hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh limit at infinity hai: \(x\) bohat bara negative number banta ja raha hai (\(-100, -1000, -1000000, \ldots\)).
\(x^2\) phir bhi positive aur bohat bara hota hai, is liye upar neeche dono bare: \(\infty/\infty\).
Plan: har term ko \(x^2\) se divide, phir \(\frac{c}{x} \to 0\) aur \(\frac{c}{x^2} \to 0\). Yeh Q1 ke sequences jaisa hi hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{x^2 + 5x + 4}{x^2 + 3x - 4}\), \(x \to -\infty\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Upar aur neeche ko \(x^2\) (denominator ki sab se bari power) se divide karna (12.2.5).

Har term ko \(x^2\) se divide karein
\[\frac{x^2 + 5x + 4}{x^2 + 3x - 4} = \frac{1 + \dfrac{5}{x} + \dfrac{4}{x^2}}{1 + \dfrac{3}{x} - \dfrac{4}{x^2}}\]
Kyun: Value nahi badli, lekin ab har barhne wali term ya to \(1\) ban gayi ya aisi term jis ke neeche \(x\) hai.

Ab \(x \to -\infty\) karein
\[\lim_{x \to -\infty} \frac{x^2 + 5x + 4}{x^2 + 3x - 4} = \frac{1 + 0 + 0}{1 + 0 - 0}\]
\[= 1\]
Kyun: Fixed number ko bohat bare negative number se divide karo to bhi jawab chhota hota hai, jaise \(\frac{5}{-1000} = -0.005\). Is liye \(\frac{5}{x}\), \(\frac{4}{x^2}\), \(\frac{3}{x}\) sab zero ki taraf.
Dhyan dein: \(x \to -\infty\) mein bhi \(\frac{c}{x} \to 0\) hi hota hai; sign se zero par koi farq nahi parta.

Tasdeeq
\[x = -1000:\ \frac{995004}{996996} \approx 0.998\]
Kyun: \(1\) ke qareeb. Degree barabar ho to jawab leading coefficients ki nisbat \(1/1 = 1\) hota hai, yeh bhi mil gaya.

blocks.explanation:
\(x = 1\) par \(0/0\), is liye \((x - 1)\) common factor hai. Yeh bilkul Q3 jaisa algebraic sawal hai.
Plan: upar difference of cubes, neeche difference of squares, \((x - 1)\) kaatna, phir value rakhna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{x^3 - 1}{x^2 - 1}\), \(x \to 1\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Factorise kar ke common factor \((x - 1)\) kaatna.

Pehle seedha value rakh kar dekhein
\[\text{Top: } 1 - 1 = 0, \quad \text{Bottom: } 1 - 1 = 0\]
Kyun: \(0/0\) undecided hai, aur factor theorem batata hai ke \((x - 1)\) dono ka factor hai.

Upar aur neeche factorise karein
\[x^3 - 1 = (x - 1)(x^2 + x + 1)\]
\[x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1)\]
Kyun: Difference of cubes \(a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)\) aur difference of squares \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\), jahan \(a = x\), \(b = 1\).

Kaatein aur value rakhein
\[\lim_{x \to 1} \frac{x^2 + x + 1}{x + 1} = \frac{1 + 1 + 1}{1 + 1}\]
\[= \frac{3}{2}\]
Kyun: \(x \ne 1\), is liye \(x - 1 \ne 0\) aur kaatna jaiz hai. Ab neeche \(2\) hai, zero nahi.
Dhyan dein: \(x^3 - 1\) ko \((x - 1)^3\) samajhna ghalat hai; \((x - 1)^3 = x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x - 1\) hota hai.

Tasdeeq
\[x = 1.01:\ \frac{0.030301}{0.0201} \approx 1.5075\]
Kyun: \(3/2 = 1.5\) ke qareeb. Q3(ix) ka formula \(\frac{n}{m}a^{n-m}\) bhi \(n = 3\), \(m = 2\), \(a = 1\) par \(\frac{3}{2}\) deta hai: do tareeqon se ek hi jawab.

blocks.explanation:
\(t \to 0\) par dono fractions bohat bare ho jate hain, yani \(\infty - \infty\): yeh bhi undecided form hai, kyunke do bare numbers ka farq kuch bhi ho sakta hai.
Plan: dono ko ek fraction banayenge (jo \(0/0\) shakal dega), phir \(1 + \sqrt{1 + t}\) se rationalise, \(t\) kaatna, aur value rakhna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\dfrac{1}{t\sqrt{1 + t}} - \dfrac{1}{t}\), \(t \to 0\).
Humein find karna hai: is ka limit.
Tareeqa: Common denominator le kar ek fraction banana, phir numerator ko rationalise kar ke common factor \(t\) kaatna.

Ek fraction banayein
\[\frac{1}{t\sqrt{1 + t}} - \frac{1}{t} = \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 + t}}{t\sqrt{1 + t}}\]
Kyun: Common denominator \(t\sqrt{1 + t}\) hai. Doosre fraction ko \(\sqrt{1 + t}\) se upar neeche multiply kiya to woh \(\frac{\sqrt{1 + t}}{t\sqrt{1 + t}}\) bana. Ab \(t = 0\) par upar \(1 - 1 = 0\) aur neeche \(0\): \(0/0\).

Numerator ko rationalise karein
\[= \frac{(1 - \sqrt{1 + t})(1 + \sqrt{1 + t})}{t\sqrt{1 + t}\,(1 + \sqrt{1 + t})}\]
\[= \frac{1 - (1 + t)}{t\sqrt{1 + t}\,(1 + \sqrt{1 + t})}\]
\[= \frac{-t}{t\sqrt{1 + t}\,(1 + \sqrt{1 + t})}\]
Kyun: \((1 - \sqrt{1 + t})(1 + \sqrt{1 + t}) = 1 - (1 + t) = -t\): root ghaib aur \(t\) saamne aa gaya, jo neeche wale \(t\) ke saath katega.
Dhyan dein: \(1 - (1 + t)\) mein bracket ka minus dono terms par lagta hai: \(1 - 1 - t = -t\).

\(t\) kaat kar \(t = 0\) rakhein
\[\lim_{t \to 0} \frac{-1}{\sqrt{1 + t}\,(1 + \sqrt{1 + t})} = \frac{-1}{1(1 + 1)}\]
\[= -\frac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(t \ne 0\), is liye kaatna jaiz hai. Ab neeche \(1 \times 2 = 2\) hai, zero nahi. Upar wala minus sign jawab mein rehta hai.

Tasdeeq
\[t = 0.01:\ \frac{1}{0.01\sqrt{1.01}} - 100 \approx -0.4963\]
Kyun: \(-1/2\) ke qareeb, aur sign bhi negative: jawab sahi hai.
